```{r setup}
library(adorn)
```

These examples use the `timed`, `logged` and `memoize` decorators from
`vignette("examples_01")`, repeated here so this vignette stands alone. The
`memoize` here is a minimal version that keys on the raw arguments and needs no
other packages; `vignette("examples_01")` has a fuller one.

```{r timed}
timed <- decorator(
  function(f, ..., digits = 3) {
    name <- decorator_context()$name
    start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
    on.exit(message(sprintf(
      "%s took %s s",
      name,
      round(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - start, digits)
    )))
    f(...)
  }
)

slow_add <- timed %@%
  function(x, y = 1) {
    Sys.sleep(0.1)
    x + y
  }
slow_add(2)
```

```{r logged}
logged <- decorator(
  function(f, ...) {
    name <- decorator_context()$name
    message("-> ", name)
    result <- withVisible(f(...))
    message("<- ", name)
    if (result$visible) result$value else invisible(result$value)
  }
)

double <- logged %@% function(x) x * 2
double(21)
```

```{r memoize}
memoize <- decorator(
  function(f) {
    cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    function(...) {
      key <- paste(deparse(list(...)), collapse = "")
      if (!exists(key, envir = cache, inherits = FALSE)) {
        assign(key, f(...), envir = cache)
      }
      get(key, envir = cache, inherits = FALSE)
    }
  }
)

fib <- memoize %@% function(n) if (n < 2) n else fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
fib(30)
```

# Decorating methods of classes that already exist

`%@%` is for methods you are defining. This vignette is about the other case:
the class is already built, perhaps by another package, and you want to wrap
one of its methods afterwards.

## S7

Start with a class and a generic, each with a method already registered.

```{r s7-setup}
library(S7)

Dog <- new_class("Dog", properties = list(name = class_character))

speak <- new_generic("speak", "x")
method(speak, Dog) <- function(x) paste(x@name, "says woof")

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

`decorate()` takes the generic and the class, and wraps the registered method
in place.

```{r s7-decorate}
decorate(speak, timed, class = Dog)

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

Each call adds a layer on the outside, and `decorators()` shows the stack of
the current method, outermost first.

```{r s7-stack}
decorate(speak, logged, class = Dog)

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
decorators(method(speak, Dog))
```

The replacement form mirrors `method(generic, class) <- fn`:

```{r s7-replace}
decorate(speak, Dog) <- memoize

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

`undecorate()` returns the original function, which you can register again to
remove all the decorators.

```{r s7-undecorate}
method(speak, Dog) <- undecorate(method(speak, Dog))

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

## R6

`decorate()` takes the class generator and the name of the method. Objects
created afterwards use the decorated method.

```{r r6-setup, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
library(R6)

Counter <- R6Class(
  "Counter",
  public = list(
    n = 0,
    add = function(k = 1) {
      self$n <- self$n + k
      invisible(self)
    },
    reset = function() {
      self$n <- 0
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)
```

```{r r6-decorate, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
decorate(Counter, logged, method = "add")

counter <- Counter$new()
counter$add(2)$add(3)
counter$n
```

The decorated method still sees `self`, and `invisible(self)` still chains.

Objects created *before* the call keep the old method, because R6 copies
methods into each object when it is created. Decorate before you create
objects.

### Several methods, private and active methods

Pass several names to `method`. Use `where` for methods that are not public
(`"public"` is the default, the others are `"private"` and `"active"`).

```{r r6-where, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
Safe <- R6Class(
  "Safe",
  public = list(go = function() private$step()),
  private = list(step = function() "ok")
)

decorate(Safe, logged, method = "step", where = "private")
Safe$new()$go()
```

### Inherited methods

A method the class only inherits is copied into the class you pass and
decorated there. The parent class is not changed, which matches what
`decorate()` does for S7.

```{r r6-inherit, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
Doubler <- R6Class("Doubler", inherit = Counter)

decorate(Doubler, timed, method = "reset")

invisible(Doubler$new()$reset())   # timed
invisible(Counter$new()$reset())   # not timed
```

The copy is a snapshot: if you decorate `Counter$reset` again later, `Doubler`
keeps the version it copied.

### Replacement form

For public methods you can also write it the way S7 writes
`method(generic, class) <- fn`.

```{r r6-replace, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
decorate(Counter, "reset") <- logged

invisible(Counter$new()$reset())
```

### Stateful decorators

For a stateful decorator like `memoize`, remember the cache belongs to the
class, so every object shares it.

```{r r6-memoize, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
Model <- R6Class(
  "Model",
  public = list(
    scale = 10,
    predict = function(x) {
      message("computing")
      x * self$scale
    }
  )
)

decorate(Model, memoize, method = "predict")

m <- Model$new()
m$predict(2)
m$predict(2)
```
